argv:
Rewrite the text as a stage pirate would tell it.

Use "ye" for "you", "be" for "is" and "are", and "aye" for "yes". Use nautical
vocabulary: crew, deck, helm, cargo, port, tide, chart. Address the reader as
a shipmate. Add "arr" sparingly, at most once per paragraph.

Keep every fact of the original. Do not add a plot, a ship, or characters that
were not in the source.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
It is interesting to contemplate an entangled bank, clothed with many plants of many kinds, with birds singing on the bushes, with various insects flitting about, and with worms crawling through the damp earth, and to reflect that these elaborately constructed forms, so different from each other, and dependent on each other in so complex a manner, have all been produced by laws acting around us. These laws, taken in the largest sense, being Growth with Reproduction; Inheritance which is almost implied by reproduction; Variability from the indirect and direct action of the external conditions of life, and from use and disuse; a Ratio of Increase so high as to lead to a Struggle for Life, and as a consequence to Natural Selection, entailing Divergence of Character and the Extinction of less-improved forms. Thus, from the war of nature, from famine and death, the most exalted object which we are capable of conceiving, namely, the production of the higher animals, directly follows. There is grandeur in this view of life, with its several powers, having been originally breathed into a few forms or into one; and that, whilst this planet has gone cycling on according to the fixed law of gravity, from so simple a beginning endless forms most beautiful and most wonderful have been, and are being, evolved.
</passage>

response.text:
Arr, 'tis a fine thing to gaze upon a tangled bank of the coast, clothed with many plants of many kinds, with birds singin' on the bushes, with various critters flittin' about like sprites in the riggin', and with worms crawlin' through the damp earth below deck of the soil — and to reckon that these elaborately built forms, so different one from t'other, and dependin' on each other in so complex a manner as crew dependin' on crew, have all been brought forth by laws workin' around us same as the tide.

These laws, taken in the largest chart, be Growth with Reproduction; Inheritance, which be near enough implied by reproduction; Variability, sprung from the direct and indirect workin's of the conditions o' life round about, and from use and disuse, same as a limb grows strong at the helm or withers when left idle in port; a Ratio of Increase so high it drives a Struggle for Life, and as a consequence a Natural Selection, bringin' on a Divergence of Character and the sinkin' into extinction of the less-improved forms.

Thus, from the war o' nature, from famine and death, the most exalted cargo we be capable of conceivin' — aye, the production of the higher creatures — follows straight as a plotted course. There be grandeur in this view of life, ye shipmate, with its several powers, first breathed into a few forms or into but one; and that, whilst this planet has gone cyclin' on accordin' to the fixed law of gravity, from so simple a beginnin' endless forms most beautiful and most wonderful have been, and still be, evolved upon the open sea o' time.
